description: Compare pan volumes from dimensions, then scale every ingredient by the exact ratio — plus a batter-fill check.

faqs.a: Volume of pan B divided by volume of pan A. Round pans use π·(d/2)²·depth; square/rectangular pans use length × width × depth.
faqs.q: How is the scaling factor calculated?

faqs.a: Aim to fill a pan between one-half and two-thirds full. Below half the cake may overbake and dry out; above two-thirds the batter can overflow or dome badly.
faqs.q: How full should I fill the pan?

faqs.a: Change the shape and the dimensions of the second pan. Use the depth field to match tall (3 in) versus standard (2 in) pans.
faqs.q: What if my pans have different depths?
